docs.title: pymorsed
docs.text: Python library for encoding, decoding, generating, and analyzing Morse code audio signals.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Text to Morse conversion
  • Morse to Text conversion
  • Multi-language support
  • Morse Audio Signal generation
  • Morse Audio Signal decoding from file
  • Waveform visualization

docs.title: Supported Languages
docs.text:
Language Code English english Russian russian Hindi hindi

Example:

from pymorsed.utils import load_language

mapping = load_language("russian")

Tip

Additional language mappings will be added in future releases.

docs.title: API Reference
docs.text: This page documents all public functions provided by the pymorsed library.

docs.title: Encoder Module
docs.text: from pymorsed.encoder import encode

docs.title: encode(text, language="english")
docs.text: Converts plain text into Morse code.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Description text str Text to encode into Morse code language str Language mapping to use ("english", "russian")

docs.title: Returns
docs.text:
str

Morse code representation of the input text.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
from pymorsed.encoder import encode

morse = encode("HELLO")
print(morse)

Output:

.... . .-.. .-.. ---

docs.title: Decoder Module
docs.text: from pymorsed.decoder import decode

docs.title: decode(morse, language="english")
docs.text: Converts Morse code back into plain text.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Description morse str Morse code string language str Language mapping used during decoding

docs.title: Returns
docs.text:
str

Decoded text.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
from pymorsed.decoder import decode

text = decode(".... . .-.. .-.. ---")
print(text)

Output:

HELLO

docs.title: play_audio(audio)
docs.text: Plays a generated Morse code waveform through the system speakers.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type audio numpy.ndarray

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: None

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
from pymorsed.audio_encoder import *

audio = morse_to_audio("... --- ...")
play_audio(audio)

docs.title: save_audio(audio, filename, fs=44100)
docs.text: Saves a Morse waveform as a WAV file.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Description audio numpy.ndarray Audio waveform filename str Output filename fs int Sample rate

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: None

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
from pymorsed.audio_encoder import *

audio = morse_to_audio("... --- ...")
save_audio(audio, "sos.wav")

docs.title: plot_waveform(audio, fs=44100)
docs.text: Displays the waveform using Matplotlib.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type audio numpy.ndarray fs int

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: None

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
from pymorsed.audio_encoder import *

audio = morse_to_audio("... --- ...")
plot_waveform(audio)

docs.title: Audio Decoder Module
docs.text: from pymorsed.audio_decoder import decode_from_file

docs.title: decode_from_file(filepath)
docs.text:
Decodes Morse code from a WAV audio file.

The decoder performs:

  1. Audio loading
  2. Stereo-to-mono conversion
  3. Silence trimming
  4. Envelope extraction
  5. Signal smoothing
  6. Thresholding
  7. Morse symbol reconstruction
  8. Text decoding

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Description filepath str Path to WAV file

docs.title: Returns
docs.text:
str

Decoded text.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
from pymorsed.audio_decoder import decode_from_file

text = decode_from_file("sos.wav")
print(text)

Output:

SOS

docs.title: Exceptions
docs.text:
May raise:

FileNotFoundError

If the audio file does not exist.

RuntimeError

If decoding fails due to invalid audio data.

docs.title: Top-Level Imports
docs.text:
The package exposes commonly used functions directly from the root package.

from pymorsed import encode
from pymorsed import decode
from pymorsed import morse_to_audio

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
from pymorsed import encode, decode

morse = encode("HELLO")
text = decode(morse)

print(morse)
print(text)

Output:

.... . .-.. .-.. ---
HELLO

docs.title: Command-Line Interface
docs.text:
The pymorsed CLI provides a convenient way to use Morse-code functionality directly from the terminal.

Quick Start

Install the package and check the available commands:

pip install pymorsed
pymorsed --help

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Install the latest release from PyPI:

pip install pymorsed

After installation, verify that the CLI is available:

pymorsed --help

Note

The pymorsed command is installed automatically with the package.

docs.title: Basic Usage
docs.text:
The general syntax is:

pymorsed <command> [arguments]

For example:

pymorsed encode-audio "HELLO WORLD"

To see the options available for any command:

pymorsed <command> --help

docs.title: Audio Commands
docs.text: The audio commands allow you to convert between text and Morse-code audio.

docs.title: encode-audio
docs.text: Convert text into a Morse-code audio signal and play the generated audio. The audio can optionally be saved to a file using the -o or --output option.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: pymorsed encode-audio <text> [-o <output_file>]

docs.title: Arguments and Options
docs.text: Argument / Option Required Description text Yes Text to convert into Morse-code audio. -o, --output No Save the generated audio to the specified file.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Encode a single word:

pymorsed encode-audio "HELLO"

This converts HELLO to Morse code and plays the generated audio.

Encode text without quotation marks:

pymorsed encode-audio HELLO

Using multiple words

Put text containing spaces inside quotation marks.

pymorsed encode-audio "SOS HELP"

docs.title: Saving the Generated Audio
docs.text:
Use -o or --output to save the generated audio to a file.

pymorsed encode-audio "HELLO" -o hello.wav

The long form can also be used:

pymorsed encode-audio "HELLO" --output hello.wav

If no output option is provided, the generated audio is only played and is not saved.

docs.title: Supported Output Formats
docs.text:
The output format is determined by the file extension. Supported formats include:

  • .wav
  • .flac
  • .ogg
  • .mp3

You do not need to provide the file extension explicitly. If no extension is provided, .wav is used by default.

For example:

pymorsed encode-audio "SOS" -o sos

saves the audio as:

output/sos.wav

You can also explicitly specify a supported extension:

pymorsed encode-audio "SOS" -o sos.wav

pymorsed encode-audio "SOS" -o sos.flac

Unsupported formats

An unsupported file extension will result in an error. Use one of the supported audio formats when specifying --output.

docs.title: Command Help
docs.text:
To view the available arguments and options:

pymorsed encode-audio --help

docs.title: decode-audio
docs.text: Convert Morse-code audio into text.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: pymorsed decode-audio <audio_file_path>

docs.title: Argument
docs.text: Argument Required Description audio_file_path Yes Path to the audio file containing Morse code.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
pymorsed decode-audio "E://audios/morse.wav"

The command reads the Morse-code signal from the audio file and outputs the decoded text.

docs.title: Command Help
docs.text: pymorsed decode-audio --help

docs.title: Help and Discoverability
docs.text: The CLI provides help at both the global and command levels.

docs.title: Global Help
docs.text:
Use:

pymorsed --help

This displays the available commands and global options.

docs.title: Command-Specific Help
docs.text:
Use:

pymorsed encode-audio --help

or:

pymorsed decode-audio --help

This displays the syntax, arguments, and description for the selected command.

Not sure what to use?

Start with pymorsed --help and then open the help page for the command you want to use.

docs.title: Command Reference
docs.text: Command Description pymorsed --help Display general CLI help. pymorsed encode-audio <text> Convert text to Morse-code audio. pymorsed decode-audio <audio_file_path> Decode Morse-code audio into text. pymorsed <command> --help Display help for a specific command.

docs.text: pymorsed encode-audio "SOS"

docs.title: Encode a sentence
docs.text: pymorsed encode-audio "HELLO WORLD"

docs.title: Decode an audio file

docs.title: CLI Architecture
docs.text:
The CLI is implemented using Python's argparse module.

The command structure follows a subcommand-based design:

pymorsed
│
├── encode
│
├── decode
│
├── encode-audio
│   ├── text
│   └── -o, --output
│
└── decode-audio
    └── audio_file

Each subcommand has its own parser and arguments. This provides:

  • Clear command organization
  • Command-specific help
  • Argument validation
  • Easy extension for future commands

Design principle

The CLI separates the command interface from the underlying Morse-code functionality. This allows the same library functionality to be used both programmatically from Python and interactively from the terminal.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
The recommended way is to import directly from the package namespace.

from pymorsed import encode, decode, morse_to_audio

morse = encode("HELLO")
print(morse)

text = decode(morse)
print(text)

docs.title: Morse Code Spacing Rules
docs.text: pymorsed follows standard Morse code spacing conventions when encoding and decoding messages.

docs.title: Letter Separation
docs.text:
Individual Morse symbols within a letter are written together without spaces.

Examples:

Character Morse Code A .- B -... S ... O ---

docs.title: Word Separation
docs.text:
Letters are separated by a single space.

Example:

HELLO

becomes:

.... . .-.. .-.. ---

Notice that each Morse letter is separated by one space.

docs.title: Multiple Words
docs.text:
Words are separated using the forward slash character (/).

Example:

HELLO WORLD

becomes:

.... . .-.. .-.. --- / .-- --- .-. .-.. -..

The slash represents a word boundary.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
Morse Pattern Meaning . Dot - Dash Space () Separates letters Slash (/) Separates words

Note

When manually providing Morse code to `decode()`, use a single space between letters and a forward slash (`/`) between words.

docs.text: You can also import functionality from specific modules.

from pymorsed.encoder import encode

docs.text:

docs.title: Audio Encoding
docs.text:
from pymorsed.audio_encoder import morse_to_audio

morse_to_audio("... --- ...")

docs.title: Audio Decoding
docs.text:
from pymorsed.audio_decoder import decode_from_file

text = decode_from_file("sos.wav")

docs.title: Import the Entire Package
docs.text:
import pymorsed

morse = pymorsed.encode("HELLO")
text = pymorsed.decode(morse)

This approach is useful when working with multiple functions from the library.
